extraction.name: Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training
extraction.description: Common Corpus is the largest open dataset for language model pre-training, containing about two trillion tokens of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data. It includes a wide variety of languages, ranging from main European languages to low-resource ones, and a large portion of code data. The dataset is designed to be compliant with AI legislation and data security regulations, providing a critical infrastructure for open science research in LLMs.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled from various open sources, including public domain texts, permissively licensed content, and curated collections. Data sources include Wikimedia projects (Wikipedia, Wikisource), YouTube Commons, StackExchange, OpenAlex, The Stack v1 and v2, and multiple cultural heritage institutions (e.g., Library of Congress, French National Library, Europeana). The collection process involved manual curation, API-based retrieval, and domain-specific filtering to ensure compliance with licensing and quality standards.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data sources include public domain texts, permissively licensed content, and curated collections from institutions such as Wikimedia projects, YouTube Commons, StackExchange, OpenAlex, The Stack v1 and v2, and multiple cultural heritage institutions (e.g., Library of Congress, French National Library, Europeana).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 1946-2024 (varies by collection; e.g., Finance Commons: mid-20th century to 2024, Open Culture: 18th-19th centuries to present, Open Science: varies by dataset)
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data was filtered to remove non-permissible licenses, low-quality content, and non-informative files (e.g., SVG, CSV, JSON). Manual filters were applied to discard low-quality code data, and files with excessive digits were removed. OCR correction tools (OCRonos) were used to improve digitization quality.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset underwent extensive preprocessing, including text segmentation (Segmentext), OCR error detection (OCRoscope, OCRerrcr), OCR correction (OCRonos), PII removal (using Microsoft Presidio), and toxicity filtering (Celadon). Metadata was standardized, and documents were filtered by license, language, and domain.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were not explicitly described in the paper, but the dataset includes metadata such as license, language, domain, and creation year for each document. Toxicity classification was performed using a multilingual toxicity classifier (Celadon) trained on 2M annotated samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Celadon (a DeBERTa-v3-small model) for toxicity classification; Presidio for PII removal; Segmentext for text segmentation; OCRoscope and OCRerrcr for OCR error detection; OCRonos for OCR correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Toxicity filtering was performed using a multilingual classifier (Celadon) trained on 2M annotated samples, identifying harmful content across five dimensions (race, gender, religion, ability, violence). PII was replaced with fictitious but realistic values to preserve text integrity.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Celadon (toxicity classifier), Presidio (PII removal), Segmentext (text segmentation), OCRoscope (OCR error detection), OCRerrcr (OCR error detection), OCRonos (OCR correction)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus is an evolving resource with continuous updates and archiving of past versions for reproducibility. The dataset is hosted on HuggingFace, ensuring proper archiving and versioning. Future expansions include collecting more data in European and African languages (e.g., Swahili, Wolof, Bambara).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: PII (e.g., phone numbers, email addresses, IP addresses) was identified and replaced with fictitious but realistic values to comply with GDPR and other regulations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to support open science research in LLMs while adhering to legal and ethical standards. It provides a critical infrastructure for training models in compliance with AI legislation, particularly in the EU. The dataset also enables the development of multilingual and multimodal models, as well as historical and creative writing models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes historical texts that may contain harmful language or biases reflective of past cultural norms. Toxicity filtering (Celadon) was applied to mitigate these issues. The dataset also aims to address biases in low-resource languages by including diverse language sources.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Common Corpus does not cover the entire range of available open data (open data paradox). Coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow, and the dataset is not suitable for instruction-tuning or specialized tasks. OCR errors and other digitization artifacts may persist despite correction efforts. The dataset is primarily focused on European languages, with limited coverage of non-European languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is designed for pre-training LLMs in compliance with legal and ethical standards. It can be used for developing multilingual, multimodal, and historical language models, as well as creative writing and legal/financial domain models.
